MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 22, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Ambassador High School student intern Sarah Yonemura.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Development/PW Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JUNE & JULY 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68616 THROUGH 68668 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $448,511.09 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070125 THROUGH
  070625 IN THE AMOUNT OF $663,913.23; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $1,112,424.32 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 24, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 15, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  2025 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DEBRIEF

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 22, 2025
 F.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS' JUNE BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Ambassador High School student intern Sarah Yonemura provided a presentation outlining
her experience during her summer internship at City Hall, including the new speaker card
sign she designed at the entrance of the Council Chamber.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250169
  AMENDMENT AND RESTATEMENT OF CHAPTER 17.56 OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO ACCESSORY
  DWELLING UNITS
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing for Ordinance No.
  752; 2) Take public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues related to Zoning Text Amendment
  ZTA-250205; 4) Introduce for first reading, Ordinance No. 752; and 5) Continue the
  Public Hearing for a second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 752, to the City
  Council meeting of August 12, 2025.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, to
  open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Written public testimony was received from the California Housing Defense Fund (CalHDF),
identifying a small number of additional items that CalHDF believes the City should correct
before finalizing its proposed ordinance. Community Development and Public Works Director
Naughton explained that the City is in the process of updating its objective design guidelines
and standards to align with State law, and noted that the City has never denied an application
for an ADU. Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton further explained
that these concerns would be addressed before the adoption of the Ordinance on August 26,
2025.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, to close the public hearing.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 752 AND CONTINUE
  THE PUBLIC HEARING FOR A SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF
  ORDINANCE NO. 752, TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF AUGUST 26,
  2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 752 by title.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 250169
  AMENDMENT OF CHAPTERS 16.06 AND 17.80 OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO URBAN LOT SPLITS AND URBAN
  DWELLING UNITS
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 22, 2025
   Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Take public testimony; 2) Discuss
  Ordinance No. 753; 3) Close the public hearing; and 4) Conduct the second reading
  and adopt Ordinance No. 753.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, to open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, to close the public hearing.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONDUCT THE SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 753.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 753 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO SEQUEL CONTRACTORS, INC. FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 ANNUAL STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Award the bid to Sequel Contractors Inc.
  in the amount of $1,318,845.00, plus a 10% contingency ($131,885.00) for a grand
  total of $1,450,730.00; and 2) Approve Task Order Number 2025-16 in the amount of
  $135,480 under Willdan Engineering’s Master Professional Services Agreement,
  approved as to form by the City Attorney.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER encouraged staff to complete the project as soon as
possible to lessen the impact on traffic in the area due to tutoring services and the library.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AWARD THE BID TO SEQUEL CONTRACTORS INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,318,845.00, PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY ($131,885.00) FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL OF $1,450,730.00.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER NUMBER 2025-16 IN THE AMOUNT OF $135,480
  UNDER WILLDAN ENGINEERING’S MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT, APPROVED AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 22, 2025
   ABSENT:  Schmitz

B.  TASK ORDER WITH CITYGREEN CONSULTING FOR SB 1383 COMPLIANCE
  ASSISTANCE
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Task Order No. 2025-02 with
  CityGreen Consulting, under the existing Master Professional Services Agreement,
  in an amount not to exceed $20,680 for continued SB 1383 compliance assistance.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Manager Graham explained that this is the fifth year the City has had to comply
with Senate Bill 1383, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public Works Manager Graham explained that this Task Order will assist staff with some of
the reporting challenges the City faces in complying with SB 1383, in response to MAYOR
STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER NO. 2025-02 WITH CITYGREEN CONSULTING,
  UNDER THE EXISTING MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT, IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $20,680 FOR CONTINUED
  SB 1383 COMPLIANCE ASSISTANCE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: WALL OF RECOGNITION
  PLAQUE - DAVID WAHBA

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the addition of a bronze plaque to
  the recognition wall honoring David Wahba’s tenure with the City.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR STEGURA called for a motion by acclimation. COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER moved, as follows:

  APPROVE THE ADDITION OF A BRONZE PLAQUE TO THE RECOGNITION
  WALL HONORING DAVID WAHBA’S TENURE WITH THE CITY.

MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

D.  FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 WORKPLAN

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 22, 2025
 There being no objection, MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Cal Cities State Board of Directors meeting last week
in San Jose.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER will be attending the Cal Water Emergency Operations
Center training on July 31.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance Board meeting and South Bay Cities
Council of Governments Board of Directors meeting, as well as the Los Angeles County
Sanitation District Board meeting.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:42 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory of COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ’s mother, Lydia Hernandez, as well as the three Los Angeles County Sheriff
Deputies who were tragically killed in a deadly explosion that occurred at the LASD training
facility in East Los Angeles: Deputy Joshua Kelley-Eklund, Deputy Victor Lemus, and Deputy
William Osborn.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JULY 22, 2025
